title: Per-action toast feedback must stay independent of shared validation/banner state
answers: Why does the drop still show a toast even when the config is invalid?
Should per-file upload feedback depend on the overall dry-run result?
How should success confirmation relate to a shared error banner?
body:
Symptom: Users could not tell if a drag-and-drop onto a dropzone succeeded, because the only shared signal (the dry-run validation banner) could show the same warning/error regardless of whether this particular drop worked.
Root cause: onDrop handlers only updated form state and re-ran the shared dry-run validation (public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/import-to-gma/steps/Step1AlertmanagerResources.tsx:Step1Content), giving no per-action acknowledgement.
Fix pattern: Fire a `notifyApp.success(...)` toast directly inside each onDrop callback, independent of the shared validation/banner state, so it confirms the local action succeeded even when the banner reports an unrelated warning or error.
Constraints: Use this pattern when a UI has a shared status indicator (banner, validation summary) that doesn't reflect the success of discrete sub-actions (file drops, item adds); don't use it to replace validation errors themselves, which still belong in the banner.
applies: Multi-step forms/wizards with discrete add/drop actions plus a shared validation banner (e.g. import-to-gma wizard Step 1).

search: Multi-step forms with discrete add/drop actions and a shared validation banner must fire per-action toast feedback independently by calling notifyApp.success() directly inside each onDrop callback, not relying on the shared banner to confirm individual actions. The shared validation state (banner or dry-run result) often reports unrelated warnings or errors and gives no acknowledgement that a particular drop or add succeeded, so the per-action toast decouples action feedback from validation state. Do not use this pattern to replace validation errors themselves, which belong in the banner. This applies to multi-step wizards like the alerting import-to-gma Step 1 (public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/import-to-gma/steps/Step1AlertmanagerResources.tsx).
